video_title: AI Genius Exposes Left Wing AI Doomers
gist: Joe Lonsdale interviews Brian Chow, founder of Effort News, a four-person AI-native investigative outlet that runs 24-72 hour long-context LLM queries across federal HHS, Medicare/Medicaid and defense spending databases to surface stories no human reporter has the time to find. The headline scoop broken on the episode is not the AI-doomer story the title implies but a claimed $21 billion pool of state health programs, funded largely by federal Medicaid/Medicare dollars, that pay providers to close racial health disparities; the AI-doomer/effective-altruism media-capture investigation is one of three cases discussed alongside a UK counterterrorism analysis. The through-line is a thesis that cheap exhaustive machine search over public records collapses the cost of accountability journalism, that government (not corporate) misconduct is the under-policed side of the ledger, and that a fragmented media market is about to recentralize around provable, auditable records.

insights.claim: Effort News runs continuous 24-, 48- and 72-hour LLM queries against large central federal spending databases (HHS grant tables, Medicare/Medicaid reimbursement records, defense spending) to connect financial payment trails, an approach its founder says was technically impossible before recent long-context model improvements.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A working commercial application of multi-day agentic LLM runs over public data; investors tracking agentic-AI monetization should note that document-forensics workloads are already producing paying-subscriber output with a four-person team.
insights.quote: And we run these longunning AI queries uh 24 48 72 hours putting together connecting the dots between all these financial payments.

insights.claim: The specific capability unlock for AI-driven records journalism is long-context breakthroughs plus the ability to run models in multi-day task windows, the same capability set now being applied to open math problems and drug discovery.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Frames long-horizon agent runtime rather than raw model IQ as the commercially relevant frontier capability, a useful lens for evaluating AI infrastructure and application startups.
insights.quote: Part of it is the long context breakthroughs.

insights.claim: The economics of machine investigation invert human newsroom constraints: Effort News tolerates roughly a thousand false positives per real story because compute is cheap and only the hits require manual review, allowing exhaustive search of a full government table that no human could ever read end to end.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A transferable unit-economics model for any AI search business: value accrues where recall matters more than precision and verification is cheap relative to discovery.
insights.quote: we can have like a thousand misses for every hit and we can exhaustively search the table

insights.claim: More than 80% of news stories are solicited by a source who brings the story to the journalist, which systematically distorts what the public sees even when each individual story is genuine.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Quantifies the agenda-setting leverage of PR and advocacy operations over the news pipeline, the structural gap that machine-originated stories are designed to arbitrage.
insights.quote: more than 80% of news stories are solicited. A source comes to you, they say, I want you to run this story.

insights.claim: On narrowly objective extraction questions such as how much money entity X paid entity Y, Effort News reports that current AI models have been correct in 100% of the cases the team has manually evaluated, while all hits still get human verification before publication.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A practitioner-grade accuracy claim on structured financial extraction, the specific task class most likely to be automated first in audit, diligence and compliance workflows.
insights.quote: when it comes to an objective fact like you know how much money did X pay Y that's something where the AI models will get literally 100% of the time

insights.claim: Effort News claims a roughly $21 billion pool exists across state health programs that pays providers to reduce racial health disparities, with almost all of that money sourced from federal Medicaid and Medicare dollars.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: If enforcement action follows, managed-care organizations and provider groups with material quality-incentive revenue tied to disparity metrics face a reimbursement line item that could be restructured or withdrawn.
insights.quote: that's a total of a $21 billion pool across all these state programs, almost all of which are taking federal Medicaid and Medicare dollars

insights.claim: These racial health-equity payment incentives operate in many red states as well as blue ones, contrary to the assumption that such programs are confined to progressive jurisdictions.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Widens the potential blast radius of any federal enforcement action beyond California and the Northeast, making state-level Medicaid budget exposure harder to screen by political geography.

insights.claim: The predicted enforcement path is the DOJ civil rights division under Harmeet Dhillon opening a review of these programs and, if requirements are not met, working with CMS to cut off the federal Medicare and Medicaid funding flowing into them.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A concrete, datable catalyst chain for anyone modeling state Medicaid budgets or provider quality-bonus revenue; the funding-cutoff lever is faster and blunter than litigation.

insights.claim: These programs were not a spontaneous 2020 reaction but the output of more than a decade of groundwork in which Obamacare created health-incentive research funding that paid RAND Corporation and other NGOs to produce reports recommending racial incentive programs, which in turn funded activist salaries that lobbied the programs into existence.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A reusable template for tracing policy outcomes back to their seed grants; the same research-grant-to-advocacy-to-legislation pipeline can be screened for in other regulated sectors.

insights.claim: Massachusetts assembled a coalition of roughly one hundred NGOs to advocate for its health-equity incentive program, which became the second largest such program in the country after California's.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Identifies the two largest state-level exposures by name, the first places to look for budget and provider-revenue impact if federal enforcement lands.

insights.claim: Effort News found a Guardian article in which all six participants — the journalist, the publisher, the subject, and all three quoted experts — were funded by the same effective-altruism grant ecosystem spanning Dustin Moskovitz's Open Philanthropy (since renamed Coefficient Giving) and Jaan Tallinn's Survival and Flourishing Fund.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Suggests apparent third-party validation in AI-risk coverage can be a single funder's closed loop, so AI-policy sentiment reads should be discounted for donor concentration.
insights.quote: they funded the journalist writing the article, the publisher, the Guardian who published the article, the subject of the article, and all three fake experts quoted in the article

insights.claim: Effort News identified roughly $40 million spent so far, which it believes understates the true figure, on paying influencers, YouTube channels including Kurzgesagt, and TikTok creators, in addition to journalist salaries, to propagate AI-risk messaging.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Puts a dollar figure on the paid-narrative layer shaping AI regulation, a direct input to political risk for AI labs and compute suppliers.
insights.quote: there was this total of $40 million being spent uh so far that we know of

insights.claim: Effort News alleges that 58 of the 100 profiles in the Time 100 AI list were bought by an Open Philanthropy funded program, while Nvidia's Jensen Huang, running the most important company in the sector, was left off the list.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A concrete test of how far prestige lists in AI have been captured; treat influence rankings as a paid channel rather than a market signal.
insights.quote: So the time 100 is really the time 42 because 58 of the hundred profiles were bought by the u by one of these open philanthropy funded programs.

insights.claim: The organizers behind the recent high-profile AI-safety whistleblower episode came from a left-wing NGO staffed by ex-Hillary Clinton staffers, ex-Extinction Rebellion climate activists and a UK prison-abolition organizer, indicating the same personnel migrating from climate doom to AI doom.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Implies AI-risk activism inherits climate activism's escalation playbook, so expect similar tactics (direct action, regulatory capture campaigns) aimed at AI labs and data centers.
insights.quote: So they're going from one version of doom to another.

insights.claim: The effective-altruism community's operative concept is the infohazard — information that is true but that the public would be harmed by knowing — which later morphed into the term malinformation and mirrors the Biden White House's pressure on Facebook to censor true content.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Names the epistemic premise underlying AI precensorship policy; anticipating it helps predict where disclosure and model-transparency mandates get fought.
insights.quote: it's basically something that's true that would be bad if the public found out

insights.claim: In UK terror attacks where a motive was identified, Effort News found 97% were some form of Islamist terrorism versus 3% under even the most expansive definition of far-right or right-wing terror, and the death ratio was 97 to 3, roughly 32 to 1.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Quantifies a resource-allocation mismatch in a Western security program, a leading indicator of the political instability narrative around UK governance.
insights.quote: 97% were some form of Islamist terrorism and 3% would be even by the most expansive definition some form of far-right or right-wing terror

insights.claim: Against a roughly 32-to-1 death ratio, UK terror-related incarcerations run at about two to one between Islamist-motivated and so-called extreme-right-motivated individuals, showing enforcement diverging sharply from the underlying threat distribution.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: The gap between harm data and enforcement data is the story's evidentiary core and the kind of ratio that drives policy reversals when it becomes public.

insights.claim: UK counter-extremism programs have listed canonical political-philosophy works including John Locke, Thomas Hobbes and George Orwell's 1984 as reading that makes a person a terrorism suspect, and classify mainstream commentator Douglas Murray as extreme right.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Illustrates definitional drift in Western security classification, a reputational and regulatory risk vector for platforms and publishers operating in the UK.
insights.quote: They literally put 1984 on the list of books that made you a suspect for terrorism.

insights.claim: Effort News spent heavily on compute investigating suspected insider trading and market manipulation around a large spike in Micron stock and on Polymarket, and found nothing publishable.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A rare published null result on a popular market-manipulation suspicion; useful as counter-evidence when narratives about systematic insider trading in AI-adjacent names circulate.
insights.quote: We spent a ton of tokens looking into insider trading um either on Poly Market or with other stocks.

insights.claim: Across many investigations it has proven far harder to find corporate misconduct stories than government ones, with government programs more often overtly breaking the letter of the law, suggesting society already polices corporations more tightly than it polices the state.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Reframes where compliance alpha and headline risk actually sit: public-sector counterparties and grant-funded programs, not listed corporates, are the under-audited side.

insights.claim: A genuine two-tier legal standard exists in which financial record-keeping that would be criminal in a private company is lawful in government, exemplified by the Pentagon never having passed a single audit without anyone expecting it to.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Sets realistic expectations for anyone underwriting government-accountability outcomes: exposure drives political and funding consequences, not prosecutions.
insights.quote: no one expected the Pentagon to pass the their audits. They haven't they've literally never passed a single audit.

insights.claim: DOGE's greatest failure was a missing theory of mind about differing standards: its people went into Treasury, judged the books by private-company standards, told Congress to jail officials, and did not realize the applicable legal standard was entirely different.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A post-mortem on why the highest-profile government-efficiency effort under-delivered, and a design constraint for any successor effort or company selling into it.
insights.quote: one of the greatest failures of Doge was that they didn't have the theory of mind of how different the standards were

insights.claim: Effort News publishes null results — investigations taken to completion that found nothing — as its principal mechanism for controlling accusations of partisan fishing expeditions.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A transferable credibility mechanism for any research or media product where selection bias is the main attack surface, including sell-side and activist research.
insights.quote: one thing that we do is we publish null results

themes.theme: Media Recentralization Thesis and Business Model

insights.claim: Chow's explicitly contrarian prediction is that the fragmented media ecosystem will recentralize rather than continue splintering, because audiences are hungry for quality, the technology now makes high-effort verifiable work possible, and topics currently coded partisan will stop being partisan.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: If right, it argues for concentrated bets on a few high-trust verifiable-record outlets rather than continued proliferation of creator-economy media, inverting the last decade's investment thesis.
insights.quote: I actually think the media ecosystem will come together. People are hungering for quality and also the quality is there.

insights.claim: Effort News monetizes today through direct subscriptions at effort.new/subscribe with a four-person team, and sees a larger opportunity in selling ground-truth data and verification services rather than advertising.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Capital efficiency of a four-person outlet breaking national stories reshapes the cost structure assumptions for media startups.
insights.quote: right now we take subscribers. It's at effort.new/subscribe.

insights.claim: The larger business is becoming the ground source of truth that other organizations rely on for business and economic processes, because Fortune 500 companies typically do not know what information they hold or whether it is clean — a description Joe Lonsdale explicitly identifies as the Palantir value proposition.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow and Joe Lonsdale
insights.so_what: Positions a media company as an emerging data-infrastructure business, a category that historically commands far higher multiples than publishing.
insights.quote: when you become the ground source of truth, you become the ground source of truth for all sorts of other business processes

insights.claim: New media companies fail to break original stories not because it is impossible but because they have convinced themselves breaking news does not matter, and Effort News has found that offering to co-break a story flips their behavior immediately.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Identifies a cheap distribution strategy — supplying scoops to commentary channels — that converts an AI research capability into audience reach without building an audience from scratch.
insights.quote: if you give people the offer, they will come. If you say let's break a new story together, they'll change their mind just like that

insights.claim: Chow predicts fiscal-transparency investigation becomes the next big bipartisan issue, citing early interest from some Democratic governors motivated by the practical goal of freeing budget money for their own preferred programs.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: If transparency depoliticizes, state-level spending reviews broaden beyond red states, widening the universe of programs and contractors exposed to funding cuts.
insights.quote: I think that this has the potential to be the next big bipartisan issue.

insights.claim: The operative analogy for transparency journalism is that there is no such thing as a pro-war war documentary: once the underlying financial records are shown, very few people support the programs, so the work reads as partisan in the short term but will not be in the long term.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: A testable claim about the political durability of grant programs exposed to public documentation, relevant to the persistence risk of government-funded revenue streams.
insights.quote: there's no such thing as an a pro-war war documentary

insights.claim: Chow expects media in the coming decade to shift toward the provable record because readers will have their own AI to check claims, meaning a growing share of consumed information will be provably true or provably false.
insights.speaker: Brian Chow, founder of Effort News
insights.so_what: Reader-side verification as a commodity capability changes the competitive dynamics of publishing; outlets whose value rests on unverifiable assertion lose pricing power.
